decisions.reason: A fashion-driven devore decoration item close to the existing range carries little sunk investment or public commitment, and after three seasons its sales can no longer be blamed on temporary causes, so rotating it out costs little and needs no justification.

A transparent burnout fabric is a trend-dependent collection item with low specific investment and only routine website presentation, so management can retire it in the next collection change without having to defend an earlier decision.
This burnout decorative fabric overlaps with the firm's other burnout and devore items and involved little commitment, making it an easy candidate to drop as decorative trends move on.

Velour-like upholstery fabric is a more durable category that customers reorder, and the firm has promised reorder continuity and stocked availability, which favours keeping it despite modest investment.

A flame-retardant plain fabric serves steady demand from contract and other buyers, and the certification effort already invested plus customers' need for reorder continuity make dropping it unattractive.
A polyester satin lining is a basic staple that supports the made-to-measure sewing business and depends little on trends, so there is no compelling reason to withdraw it.
